name: Jubilant Agri and Consumer Products Ltd (JACPL)
tagline: A genuinely high-ROCE Jubilant-group niche polymer/adhesives-plus-fertilizer business with an on-track NCLT demerger (shareholder/creditor meeting held 5-Sep-2026, 1:1 entitlement into Jubilant Agri Solutions), but the community's own SOTP math (~17-20% unlock) and a mid-teens earnings-growth profile at ~26x P/E mean there is no 10x-in-2-3-years mechanism here - it is a quality-compounder-at-fair-price with a modest special-situation kicker
business_overview: JACPL (Jubilant Bhartia Group) runs three segments: Performance Polymers & Chemicals (VP-latex - India's largest producer, used in tyre-cord dipping; SPVA/ester gum - among global top-2, sold to chewing-gum makers), Consumer Adhesives/Wood Finishes (Jivanjor, Charmwood, challenger to Pidilite's ~70% share), and P&K Fertilizers (Ramban-brand SSP, ~4.44 lakh TPA, North India) plus specialty Agri-Nutrients. Demerged from Jubilant Industries Ltd in FY24 via slump sale; now itself demerging the Agri Business (fertilizers, crop nutrition, bio-products) into Jubilant Agri Solutions Ltd (JASL) - NCLT allowed the First Motion on 8-Jul-2026, the NCLT-directed shareholders'/creditors' meeting was held 5-Sep-2026, 1 JASL share per JACPL share, and the retained polymers/adhesives entity will be renamed Jubilant Industries Limited.
fundamentals_table: ROE ~27.8% TTM; ROCE ~32-37% (FY25) - well above fertilizer/adhesive peer averages

Revenue Rs 523 Cr (+18% YoY), EBITDA Rs 68 Cr (+7%, margin 13.0% vs 14.1%), PAT Rs 46 Cr (+5%); Performance Polymers & Chemicals +27%, Agri soft on weak monsoon + higher RM + elevated working capital; adhesives +16%
5yr revenue CAGR ~25% (Rs 622 Cr FY21 -> Rs 1,541 Cr FY25) but lumpy (agri seasonality/subsidy)
D/E ~0.11; gross borrowings fell Rs 162 Cr (Mar-24) -> Rs 77 Cr (Mar-25); Net Debt/EBITDA <1x, down from Debt/EBITDA 5.5x in FY19
JACPL ~26x for ~28% ROE vs Pidilite ~75x (ROE 23%), SRF ~68x (ROE 10%), Coromandel ~38x (ROE 17.5%) - cheap on a return-adjusted peer basis
fundamentals_narrative: A genuinely high-quality, sharply deleveraged, high-ROCE business (ROCE ~32-37%, D/E ~0.11) trading at a peer-relative discount (~26x P/E for ~28% ROE vs Pidilite's ~75x for 23% ROE) - the 'hidden gem' quality framing is fundamentally supported. But (1) two independent, quantified community SOTP analyses (Oct-2025 and Mar-2026) both concluded the demerger-specific unlock from prevailing prices is modest (~17-20%), not an outsized special-situations gap; and (2) the earnings-growth profile is mid-teens at best - Q1 FY27 revenue +18% but EBITDA +7% and PAT +5%, with the Agri segment a persistent drag (the very reason for the demerger). There is no mechanism for a 10x return in 2-3 years from a mid-teens compounder already at 26x P/E; the realistic case is steady compounding plus a one-time ~15-20% demerger re-rating. The demerger is on track: NCLT First Motion allowed 8-Jul-2026, the directed shareholders'/creditors' meeting was held 5-Sep-2026, 1:1 entitlement, retained entity to be renamed Jubilant Industries Ltd.
technical_read: Not independently pulled this pass. Stock in the upper half of its 52-week range (Rs 1,460 - 2,912), ~Rs 2,178.

bull_case: Genuinely high, improving return ratios (ROCE ~32-37%, ROE ~28%) with debt down sharply (Debt/EBITDA 5.5x FY19 -> <1x) - a real quality improvement

Niche B2B technical moats in two segments: India's largest VP-latex producer (tyre-cord dipping) and among global top-2 in SPVA/ester gum (chewing-gum base) - genuine technical barriers, not commodity positions
Trades at a real peer-relative discount: ~26x P/E for ~28% ROE vs Pidilite's ~75x for 23% ROE

On-track, dated demerger (NCLT First Motion 8-Jul-2026, directed meeting 5-Sep-2026, 1:1 entitlement) separating the subsidy-dependent fertilizer drag from the higher-quality polymers/adhesives franchise
Performance Polymers & Chemicals segment growing well (+27% in Q1 FY27); adhesives +16%
bear_case: No 10x-in-2-3-years mechanism: a mid-teens earnings compounder (Q1 FY27 EBITDA +7%, PAT +5%) already at ~26x P/E cannot deliver a 10x return on that horizon; the demerger unlock is quantified by two independent SOTP analyses at only ~17-20%
Consumer-adhesives segment: ~9% operating margin vs 20%+ for peers while gaining share - unresolved whether that is brand reinvestment or margin-dilutive discounting

Real information-access constraint: no concalls, thin recent rating-agency coverage - independent verification of the demerger timeline and segment economics is harder than for a typical mainboard mid-cap

Fertilizer segment structurally subsidy/policy-dependent with genuine margin volatility (weak Q1 FY27 on poor monsoon + RM + working capital); RPT with sister Jubilant-group entities warrants due diligence not done in-thread

verdict_headline: Deep-dive pass 1: a genuine high-ROCE, peer-cheap niche-polymer business with an on-track demerger - but four_box scores 3.5 only on business quality, while there is no 10x-in-2-3-years mechanism (mid-teens growth at 26x P/E, ~17-20% demerger unlock), so thesis_fit is set to neither via analyst_override; conviction held Medium on the quality-plus-modest-catalyst case
verdict_reasoning: four_box scores 3.5 (tailwind yes: on-track dated demerger; moat yes: India's-largest VP-latex + global-top-2 SPVA; valuation yes: peer-relative discount; tam weak: niche segment sizes + Pidilite dominance in adhesives). Mechanically that permits a 10x/100x label.

analyst_override applied: the return-magnitude the label implies is not achievable here. Q1 FY27 EBITDA grew 7% and PAT 5%; the business is a mid-teens compounder at best, already priced at ~26x P/E / ~7.3x book, and the demerger-specific unlock is independently quantified at ~17-20%. There is no path to a ~10x return in 2-3 years - this is 'Nesco logic': the mechanical boxes capture quality but not the size/return-magnitude reality. thesis_fit set to 'neither'.

Conviction kept at Medium: the thesis (sustained high ROCE, niche B2B moats, peer-relative cheapness, a real if modest demerger kicker) is sound as a compounder, but the adhesive-segment margin question is unresolved and information access (no concalls) limits verification.
value_chain block retained: JACPL's VP-latex/SPVA supply-chain position into tyre and chewing-gum manufacturing is a genuine technical moat even though it is not a live active_themes.json match.

value_chain.theme: Niche B2B specialty-polymer supply chains (tyre-cord reinforcement, chewing-gum base) - not a current active_themes.json entry, added because the deep read made the chain position clear
value_chain.position: India's largest VP-latex producer (tyre-cord dipping/reinforcement input for tyre and tyre-fabric manufacturers) and among the global top-2 producers of SPVA/ester gum (the chewy-backbone/binding input for chewing-gum and bubble-gum manufacturers), plus a regional #1 SSP fertilizer brand (Ramban) in UP/Uttarakhand.
value_chain.bottleneck_node: Technical/quality-certification barriers in specialty latex grades (VP) and food-grade polymer specs (SPVA/ester gum) - few dedicated global producers in either niche, unlike commodity SBR latex.
value_chain.note: The polymer/latex value-chain position (VP-latex, SPVA) is the genuine technical moat; the adhesives-segment position is structurally weaker (challenger brand against Pidilite's dominant share) and the fertilizer position is a regional-scale commodity play subject to subsidy policy, not a chain bottleneck.

drivers: VP-latex / SPVA niche pricing (structural technical-barrier margins)
agri/fertilizer subsidy timing and monsoon-linked demand (cyclical)
consumer-adhesives mix - growing but margin-dilutive at ~9%
earnings_quality.normalised_note: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin actually fell ~100 bps to 13.0% on the agri drag and adhesive dilution; the polymer segment margins are not obviously cycle-high. The risk here is margin staying capped in the low-teens as the adhesive mix rises, not mean-reversion from a peak.

growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: 5-yr revenue CAGR ~25% but with an agri-driven lumpiness (one TTM snapshot showed -15% de-growth). Q1 FY27 revenue +18% YoY but EBITDA +7% and PAT +5%; Performance Polymers +27%, agri soft. The blended earnings-growth rate is mid-single to low-double digits, not a smooth compounder.
growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: ~26x trailing needs only low-to-mid-teens EPS CAGR at a ~20-24x exit to be fair; the recent single-digit EBITDA/PAT growth is at or slightly below that, so the multiple is roughly full pending the demerger re-rating.

management_quality.capital_allocation: Used the last 3 years to deleverage hard (Debt/EBITDA 5.5x -> <1x) and reinvest in the high-ROCE polymer segment; now separating the subsidy-dependent agri drag via demerger. No unrelated diversification. No dividend. RPTs with sister Jubilant-group entities are a watch item.
management_quality.capability_ladder_note: Concentrating on the higher-value VP-latex/SPVA niches and building the Jivanjor adhesive brand up the value curve; demerger to sharpen focus

track_record.note: JACPL has only reported as a standalone entity since the FY24 demerger from Jubilant Industries, so FY24-FY26 (incl. TTM) are the verifiable window. ROCE cleared >=15% (32-37% range) in each. Revenue growth exceeded 10% in FY24 and FY25 but the agri-driven lumpiness produced a soft TTM patch, so ~2 of 3 clear BOTH tests. Short, carve-out history - do not over-weight the count.

four_box.note: Mechanically 3.5 (tailwind yes: on-track dated demerger; moat yes: India's-largest VP-latex + global-top-2 SPVA technical barriers; valuation yes: ~26x P/E for ~28% ROE vs 68-75x lower-ROE peers; tam weak: small niche segment sizes + Pidilite's ~70% adhesive-share dominance). analyst_override=true: the boxes capture business quality but not return magnitude - Q1 FY27 EBITDA grew 7% / PAT 5%, the stock is already at ~26x P/E, and the demerger unlock is independently quantified at ~17-20%, so there is no 10x-in-2-3-years mechanism. thesis_fit deliberately kept 'neither'; conviction Medium as a quality compounder with a modest special-situation kicker.
